activity.notes: Seleucus received the satrapy of Babylonia at the settlement of Triparadeisus in 320 BCE and developed it into a strong local power base. Antigonus forced him to flee Babylonia in 316/315 BCE. ATLAS therefore records the first Babylonian satrapy as 320-c.315 BCE and leaves the subsequent exile as a real interruption rather than extending the office continuously to his later return.

sources.title: Seleucus I Nicator — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary identifies Seleucus as satrap of Babylonia from 320 to 316 or 315 BCE and records his flight after conflict with Antigonus.

sources.title: SELEUCUS — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica states that Seleucus received the satrapy of Babylonia in 320 BCE and was driven out by Antigonus in 315 BCE.
